summary: Introduces Ansible's precedence rules, which decide which value wins when the same setting is defined in several places (configuration, command line, playbook keywords, variables).
questions: Why does a setting I changed not seem to take effect in Ansible?
Where can Ansible settings be defined, and how does Ansible decide which one wins?
What are Ansible's precedence rules for?

answer_card.title: Why Ansible precedence rules matter
answer_card.answer_md: Ansible lets you control connection and execution behavior from many places: configuration settings, command-line options, playbook keywords and variables. When the same setting is defined in more than one of these, **precedence rules** decide which value is used. If a change appears to be ignored, it is usually being overridden by a higher-precedence source.
